research.topic: Imposter Syndrome – “I’m not really good enough, I’m just faking it”
verified: Imposter syndrome is a persistent self‑doubt and fear of being exposed as a fraud despite evidence of competence.
A substantial proportion of high‑achieving individuals report occasional imposter feelings, and a notable minority experience chronic symptoms, though exact percentages vary across studies.
It is a psychological pattern, not a clinical diagnosis.
Chronic imposter feelings may be associated with reduced motivation and increased burnout, as observed in some high‑pressure fields, though evidence beyond medical education is limited.
Individuals experiencing imposter feelings are often high achievers and may exhibit a strong orientation toward learning, according to some studies.

sources.title: The impostor phenomenon construct in medical education: a meta-analysis of its prevalence and a critical appraisal of its measurement.

research.hook: Myth: ‘If you’re feeling like a fraud, you just need to work harder.’ Fact: Your brain is actually playing tricks on you – and no amount of extra hours will fix it.
research.tip: Keep an “Evidence Log” – write one concrete achievement after each task and review it weekly to counter the fraud narrative.
